title: Microsoft Purview DLP: block named external domains or users from SharePoint and OneDrive files
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licensing, roles and documented blocking controls are supported. Remove the unsupported generalization about using a different address, clarify the conflicting guidance on allow entries, and expand the abbreviated portal route.

claims.claim: Admins can configure Purview DLP policies to block SharePoint and OneDrive file access for specific external domains or individual users.
claims.quote: With this enhancement, admins can configure DLP policies that block file access for specific external domains or individual users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Learn says users in neither list are blocked by default when a file matches both an allow rule and a block rule.
claims.quote: If a file matches both an allow rule and a block rule, evaluation is per rule — allowed users and domains are permitted, blocked users and domains are denied, and users in neither list are blocked by default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The scenario says evaluation is per rule, while the policy reference also uses across all matching rules.
claims.quote: If a file matches both an allow rule and a block rule, evaluation is across all matching rules — allowed users and domains are permitted, blocked users and domains are denied, and users in neither list are blocked by default.

claims.claim: The scenario's intent statement says other external recipients are allowed.
claims.quote: All other external recipients are allowed.

claims.claim: A person using a different address or a different domain is not covered by an entry for the original one.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP block specific external domain user SMTP different address block domain user matching. Opened dlp-policy-reference and dlp-create-policy-spo-odb-external; neither states this generalization about alternate identities.
claims.fix: Remove 'A person using a different address or a different domain is not covered by an entry for the original one;' and retain the advice that the list needs maintaining as partners and guests change.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in: enforcement requires an administrator to configure the rule action.
claims.quote: Any item that makes it through the conditions filter has any actions that are defined in the rule applied to it. You have to configure the required options to support the action.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal route reaches the specific external domain or user action in a custom policy.
claims.quote: Select Custom from both the Categories list and the Regulations list. On the Define policy settings page, the Create or customize advanced DLP rules option should already be selected.
claims.fix: Expand the path to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Categories: Custom > Regulations: Custom > Assign admin units > Choose where to apply the policy > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > Actions > Restrict access or encrypt the content in Microsoft 365 locations > Block access for specific external domains or users'. The omitted policy-scope selections and preselected advanced-rules option do not invalidate the printed route.

claims.claim: No documented PowerShell parameter or API operation sets the specific SharePoint and OneDrive domain and user lists.
claims.quote: Searched: DlpComplianceRule external domains Block SharePoint OneDrive parameters; Set-DlpComplianceRule domain BlockAccessScope; DLP external domains Graph API. Read New-/Set-DlpComplianceRule, including RestrictAccess and MipRestrictAccess: no list-setting syntax is documented.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule has a BlockAccessScope parameter specifying the scope of the block action, rather than domain or user lists.
claims.quote: The BlockAccessScope parameter specifies the scope of the block access action. Valid values are:

claims.claim: BlockAccessScope All blocks everyone except the owner and last modifier.
claims.quote: All: Blocks access to everyone except the owner and the last modifier.

claims.claim: BlockAccessScope PerUser blocks external users.
claims.quote: PerUser: Blocks access to external users.

claims.claim: BlockAccessScope PerAnonymousUser blocks access through Anyone with the link in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: PerAnonymousUser: Blocks access to people through the "Anyone with the link" option in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Administrators select the SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts policy locations.
claims.quote: Choose where to apply the policy. Ensure that the SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts locations are selected.

claims.claim: The creating and deploying account must belong to Compliance administrator, Compliance data administrator, Information Protection, Information Protection Admin or Security administrator.
claims.quote: The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of these role groups: Compliance administrator; Compliance data administrator; Information Protection; Information Protection Admin; Security administrator

claims.claim: The scenario creates a Custom policy under Enterprise applications & devices.
claims.quote: Select Enterprise applications & devices. Select Custom from both the Categories list and the Regulations list.

claims.claim: The variant retains the main scenario's administrative scope, conditions, exclusions and incident reports.
claims.quote: All other mapping rows from the main SharePoint and OneDrive external sharing scenario — administrative scope, conditions, exclusions, incident reports, user notifications, and user overrides — are unchanged.

claims.claim: The scenario uses Social Security numbers, credit card data and the Confidential sensitivity label as content criteria.
claims.quote: We need to block sharing of SharePoint and OneDrive items containing social security numbers, credit card data, or the "Confidential" sensitivity label

claims.claim: Microsoft's procedure says to leave the policy off while building it.
claims.quote: For this policy creation procedure, leave the policy turned off. Change these settings when you deploy the policy.

claims.claim: The service description covers DLP for Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and OneDrive for Business.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) for Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and OneDrive for Business

claims.claim: Block only people outside your organization is the existing blanket external blocking alternative.
claims.quote: Access to a sensitive file is blocked as soon as it's uploaded, regardless of whether the document is shared or not for all guests.

claims.quote: Checklist: 'Turn on alerts to admins for the rule'. The only controls row covers 'Which external domains or users a DLP rule blocks from SharePoint and OneDrive files'.
